ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, line AE intersects with CD at point B, and BF $\perp$ AE. If $\angle DBE=60^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle FBD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since BF$\perp$AE,\\
it follows that $\angle$DBF + $\angle$DBE = $90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle$DBE = $60^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle$DBF = $90^\circ$ - $\angle$DBE = $30^\circ$.\\
Hence, the measure of $\angle FBD$ is $\boxed{30^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is an oblique line AE passing through point B, A is at the upper right, and E is at the lower left; another line CD also passes through point B, D is on the left side, and C is at the lower right; ray BF points from B toward the upper left. The figure marks BF as perpendicular to AE, so because E is on AE, ∠FBE is a right angle. Ray BD is located between BF and BE, and ∠DBE has been given as 60°. Reasoning: Since ∠FBE = 90°, and BD divides ∠FBE into ∠FBD and ∠DBE, ∠FBD + ∠DBE = 90°. Substituting ∠DBE = 60°, we get ∠FBD = 90° - 60° = 30°.
